findings.text: Modern capability mapping helper exposes PCI capability region mapping where caller supplies capability offset plus minimum length plus alignment plus start skew plus size cap and optional outputs for effective length and bus address, returning an I/O mapping on success or null on validation or mapping failure.

Mapping helper enforces BAR ownership and geometry before mapping: BAR index stays within standard count and inside claimed mask, capability length exceeds start and leaves at least minimum length, start plus base offset does not wrap, resulting offset meets alignment, effective length clamps to caller cap, and minimum extent neither wraps nor exceeds BAR resource length.

Mapping failures for unexpected BAR, short length, wrap around, misalignment, out of range extent and mapping allocation error are reported through device error logging with null return, while bus address output is written only after successful mapping when requested.
Queue notification query selects a queue by index through common configuration selection and then returns notification offset read from common configuration.

Queue deletion serializes list removal with device spinlock held with interrupts saved, but skips list removal entirely when queue is in reset to avoid rejoining and stray interrupts; backend deletion and info release happen outside the locked region.
Legacy queue teardown disables MSI-X vector when enabled and performs a status read to flush posted writes, then deactivates the queue by selecting it with zero address before destroying its ring.
Modern queue teardown disables MSI-X vector when enabled, releases per-queue notification mapping only when no shared notification base exists, then destroys its ring.

Bulk queue teardown walks device queue list safely, resolves admin versus indexed queue metadata, clears affinity hints and frees per-queue interrupts for dedicated non slow vectors, deletes each queue, then releases legacy interrupt, MSI-X interrupts, affinity masks, configuration vector, vector allocation and bookkeeping allocations while clearing enable flags and counts.
Vector policy enumeration offers three strategies: dedicated vector per queue, dedicated vectors with shared slow path, and fully shared queue vector.

Single MSI-X queue setup assigns no vector when no callback exists, consumes a fresh vector for dedicated policies, steers slow path queues to configuration vector, and steers remaining shared cases to shared queue vector.

Single MSI-X queue setup creates the queue then, unless shared policy or no vector or slow vector applies, registers a ring interrupt handler under a composed device plus queue name and unwinds the queue on registration failure.

MSI-X bulk setup allocates queue metadata, queries optional admin queue index, sizes vector demand from callbacks plus change interrupt with special shared count, requests vectors, then creates named queues in order and an optional admin queue with its completion callback, unwinding everything on any failure.

Legacy interrupt bulk setup allocates metadata, queries optional admin queue, registers one shared device interrupt, marks legacy interrupt enabled without per-queue vectors, creates named queues with no vector and optional admin queue, unwinding on failure.
Queue discovery prefers MSI-X dedicated, then MSI-X with shared slow path, then MSI-X fully shared, then abandons when no PCI interrupt exists, otherwise falls back to shared legacy interrupts.
Bus name accessor returns PCI device name associated with parent PCI device.

Affinity setter rejects queues without callbacks, and when MSI-X is active either clears kernel hint for null mask or copies caller mask into per-vector storage and applies it with hint; getter returns null unless per-queue vectors are active with valid non slow vector, otherwise returns kernel affinity for that vector.

Freeze path freezes virtio device then disables PCI device on success; restore path enables PCI device, enables bus mastering, then restores virtio device; suspend and resume bypass both steps when power management reports no soft reset support, otherwise delegate to freeze and restore.
Power operations table binds six power callbacks so that suspend uses suspend handler, resume uses resume handler, freeze and poweroff use freeze handler, and thaw and restore use restore handler.
PCI identifier table claims Red Hat Qumranet vendor with any device identifier, terminated by empty entry.
Device release handler frees driver container after device lifetime ends, reflecting that container including reference counting must survive until release callback.

PCI probe allocates and initializes driver container, links PCI and virtio devices, initializes queue lists and lock, enables PCI device, probes transport, enables bus mastering, registers virtio device, and on failure unwinds transport, disables device, and either drops device reference when registered or frees container directly.

Probe order depends on legacy force flag: forced legacy tries legacy first and retries modern only on missing device or memory failure, while default tries modern first and retries legacy only on missing device.
Probe initializes main device spinlock during container setup and modern wiring initializes admin queue spinlock during transport setup.
Legacy probe claims PCI device identifiers from hexadecimal one thousand through ten thirty nine inclusive and requires revision equal to virtio PCI ABI version, rejecting others as not owned.

Legacy probe prefers sixty four bit DMA mask, falls back to thirty two bit streaming plus coherent on failure, and when sixty four bit streaming succeeds limits coherent mask to thirty two plus queue address shift; failure only warns and continues.
Legacy probe requests BAR zero, maps it for I/O, derives interrupt status pointer and vendor plus device identifiers from subsystem identifiers, and releases region on mapping failure.
Legacy removal unmaps I/O base and releases BAR zero region.

Modern PCI wiring chooses between full and nodevice configuration operations based on device capability presence, installs config vector plus queue setup plus queue teardown plus admin index handlers, copies interrupt status and identifier, and initializes admin queue lock.

Modern probe claims PCI device identifiers from hexadecimal one thousand through ten seventy nine inclusive; identifiers below ten forty derive virtio device identifier from PCI subsystem device identifier while at or above derive it as PCI identifier minus ten forty; vendor always derives from subsystem vendor.

Modern probe requires common configuration capability and otherwise defers to legacy, then requires interrupt status and notification capabilities; it negotiates DMA mask with sixty four bit preference and thirty two bit fallback, requests claimed BARs, maps common and interrupt status regions, reads notification multiplier length and offset, maps entire notification region when it fits within a page including page offset else defers to per-queue mapping.
Header fallback provides legacy probe returning missing device and empty legacy removal when legacy support is unavailable.

Legacy PCI wiring records PCI device, runs legacy probe, propagates interrupt status and identifier, installs full configuration operations plus config vector and queue handlers, and marks device legacy.
